blockedReason: Live-tested TWICE and disconfirmed both ways: (1) resubmitting the BD via feed to observe the status change is unconditionally rejected as B0700 (BD ID ALREADY PRESENT) before the producer records are ever evaluated; (2) editing pru_adb.node_relationship.relationship_status_code directly (bypassing the feed entirely) produces ZERO new activity_log_entry rows after a cycle runs - confirmed via a real automated Playwright test (utils/db.brv4.ts) that seeded the change, ran a cycle, and checked activity_log_entry for RA00RA/TE00TE: none appeared. The application has no change-detection process that reacts to a direct node_relationship edit; activity_log_entry rows are only ever written by the ingestion pipeline itself while processing an uploaded feed record, and that pipeline cannot be reached for an existing BD without hitting (1). This rule is confirmed unreachable by any feed+DB combination available to this framework. Verify manually via direct DB access to activity_log_entry / node_relationship, coordinated with whoever can trigger the underlying business logic outside the LNA feed path. [Reconfirmed on a freshly-cleaned DB, 2026-09-26: TC-BR-124 was re-run live against the clean DB and shows the identical B0700/duplicate-rejection mechanism (committed=0, rolled back=1) - a clean DB does not remove this structural conflict, since testing an update to an existing entity necessarily requires that entity to already exist from a prior submission.] [Precision correction + 3rd live data point, 2026-09-26: the B0700 duplicate-BD rejection is not an HTTP-level upload failure - the upload is accepted and the run completes normally, but the bundle is rolled back internally before any field is compared: log shows "Bundle for BD A993040100 rolled back; no records in it were applied", "0 bundle(s) committed, 1 rolled back", and critically "detectChanges found 15 of 15 extract entries unchanged - no activity record produced" - confirming the duplicate-BD check short-circuits the whole bundle before the old-vs-new field comparison this rule needs ever runs. A 3-file upload sequence (set up -> update -> revert) does not create a new path around this: file 2 (the update) hits this identical rollback, so there is nothing for a 3rd file to revert.] [3rd hypothesis tested and disconfirmed, 2026-09-26: seeded a baseline row directly into adsi_master.contract_record (permission extended for this schema specifically) keyed by a chosen SSN, then submitted ONE brand-new feed for that same SSN under a new BD/contract - reasoning that the old-vs-new comparison this rule needs might be keyed by SSN rather than contract_number, avoiding B0700 entirely since pru_adb had never seen this BD before. Result: two separate, unlinked adsi_master.contract_record rows were created for the same SSN (the seeded baseline, and a brand-new one from this feed); the new producer generated a plain AP00AP (new appointment) activity code, not RA00RA - confirming the comparison is keyed strictly by contract_number (the pru_adb-generated identifier), never by SSN. There is no way to link a pre-existing legacy baseline to a new pru_adb entity via this or any other combination available to this framework - the match only happens when the SAME contract_number is reprocessed, which is exactly the scenario B0700 blocks.] [4th hypothesis tested, 2026-09-26: per scripts/e54.json ("whether a contract already exists for the subject decides whether an appointment is created or an existing one amended"), attached an already-existing producer to a brand-new, never-before-submitted BD with a different relationship status. B0700 did not fire (new BD); the app correctly amended the existing contract (1 row, not 2) and node_relationship correctly recorded a real T-with-end-date -> A-with-no-end-date transition. However, activity_log_entry recorded AP00AP (new appointment) both times, never RA00RA. Reviewed with the user: this is expected, correct behavior, not a defect - moving a producer to a new BD is legitimately a fresh appointment event from that BD relationship's perspective, distinct from a same-BD status change. This means the technique tests a DIFFERENT scenario than BR-304 describes (same-BD status change), not BR-304 itself, and does not resolve the blocker. It also confirms the same-BD version of this test remains structurally unreachable: any second upload carrying this producer must reference a brand-new BD to avoid B0700, which is exactly what makes it a different scenario. No further feed-based avenue is apparent - this is now four independent, live-tested dead ends (feed resubmission -> B0700 rollback; direct DB edit -> no detection; SSN-keyed ADSI baseline -> unlinked, not compared; cross-BD reappointment -> correctly a different event, AP00AP not RA00RA).]

businessRuleDescription: An organisation whose relationship is terminated or inactive is recorded on the master record as eliminated, and the date the relationship ended is carried onto the master record as the elimination date.
triggerCondition:
1. Set up an organisation whose relationship status is T (or I) with a known relationship end date, differing from what the ADSI master currently shows for it (must actually change, or nothing is written).
2. Run ingestion then sync for that cycle date.
3. Authoritative check - query adsi_master.organization_record for that node: org_status should be '9' (eliminated) and org_elimination_date should equal the relationship end date. An org that stays active keeps org_status '0' and a null org_elimination_date.

Treat this only as a secondary look, not a pass/fail source - the comparator can't parse ADSIMSTR's real layout (OCCURS DEPENDING ON) and falls back to a mis-sliced 850-byte record, so its verdict for this file is unreliable by design (see CLAUDE.md's ADSIMSTR note).

triggerCondition:

- refused on its own merits, 
- set aside because an earlier record in its bundle failed,

verificationBasis:
Verify at: Control Report (CNTLRPT) counters + Skip Report (ADBSKIP) + absence from Load Output.

Remarks:
Each file answers a different question: LNAERROR = the record itself was bad, ADBSKIP reason 002 = the record was fine but something earlier in its bundle failed, ADBERROR = the record was fine but the program that writes it to ADB failed. That third case is NOT one file only - it also writes an LNAERROR line, and reaches ADBERROR only when UTP27101 reports 0002 or UTP27201 reports 0003. What identifies it is the error code (O2711 / P2721 / D2731), not which file it is in.

HOW TO TEST
1. Run one cycle on a feed with two bundles. In bundle 1, give one producer a D01 carrying SSN 000000000. That record is bad on its own (case a) and its matching D02 is then skipped through no fault of its own (case b), while the rest of the bundle still commits.
2. Bundle 2 creates case (c). Put an entity type that is not BD, LLE or HA (e.g. ZZZ) on its FIRST firm record, so that record is rejected C0716 and no office is created for the bundle. The LLE record after it is perfectly valid but has no office to attach to, so the program that creates offices (UTP27101) reports a failure. The whole bundle is then rolled back, which skips the good producer pair after it as well.
3. Look each record up by its position number in the three files below.

THE ERROR OUTPUT YOU SHOULD SEE
- File 3 LNAERROR: one line per rejected record, with the code that rejected it. A code starting C, D, E or F means the record itself was bad. Codes O2711, P2721 and D2731 mean the record was fine and a called program failed.
- File 4 ADBSKIP: one line per record that was never attempted, with a full copy of the original record so it can simply be re-fed. Reason 001 = the record type was not recognised. Reason 002 = something earlier in its bundle failed.
- File 5 ADBERROR: one block per failed program call, naming the program (UTP27101 or UTP27201) and what went wrong - 0001 the data failed a check, 0002 something in ADB it depends on is missing, 0003 a database error.

RULE IS MET WHEN: a bad record is in LNAERROR only; a skipped record is in ADBSKIP only, with reason 002 and not 001; and a failed program call is in LNAERROR with an O/P/D code AND in ADBERROR - appearing in both is correct here, not a defect.

blockedReason: This rule needs the same kind of setup as BR-022 / BR-024 / BR-034 / BR-149: a change recorded directly in the database, then waiting for the system to notice it on its own during a later, unrelated upload. We tested that exact approach on those 4 related rules and confirmed the system does not reliably pick up changes that way (see their explanations). Since this rule would require the identical technique, we did not spend further live test cycles repeating the same negative result, and are marking it BLOCKED for the same reason. Manual verification by QA/business, using a database fixture as the source workbook specifies, is required. [Reconfirmed on a freshly-cleaned DB, 2026-09-26: TC-BR-022 was re-run live against the clean DB with zero pre-existing backlog. The same 2 hand-inserted activity rows were still skipped while all 6 organic feed-driven rows from the same batch were processed together - ruling out backlog/staleness as the cause and confirming this is a structural HR2-scoping behavior, not a DB-cleanliness issue.]

blockedReason: Live-confirmed (twice, via TC-BR-304 and TC-BR-256/269) that this application has no way to observe a change to an already-committed entity: (1) resubmitting its bundle via feed to trigger the comparison is unconditionally rejected as B0700 (BD ID ALREADY PRESENT) before any field-level processing happens, and (2) directly editing the relevant table and running a cycle produces zero new activity_log_entry rows - the change-detection service (AdsiChangeDetectionService) only runs on data built from an incoming feed record during ingestion, never from a raw table scan. This rule requires observing exactly that "old vs new" comparison for an existing record, so it is unreachable by any feed+DB combination available to this framework. Verify manually via direct DB access, coordinated with the dev team on whether an update path exists outside the LNA feed. [Reconfirmed on a freshly-cleaned DB, 2026-09-26: TC-BR-124 was re-run live against the clean DB and shows the identical B0700/duplicate-rejection mechanism (committed=0, rolled back=1) - a clean DB does not remove this structural conflict, since testing an update to an existing entity necessarily requires that entity to already exist from a prior submission.]

expectedBusinessOutcome: An activity record arriving with a blank current key is an instruction to remove the subject from the master. The record is located by its prior key and deleted. 2. Remove the master row, then re-run the same delete.
